title: Ingest JSON and CSV format support
description: Extend the ingest dispatcher in memory.py with handlers for .json and .csv. JSON: expect a JSON array where each element is either a plain string (used as content) or an object with a required 'content' key and optional 'metadata' object and 'source' string; exit 1 with a descriptive error for invalid input. CSV: require --column NAME flag specifying which column holds the text; all other columns are merged into the chunk's metadata JSON; first row is the header. Add an explicit 'unsupported format' exit-1 path for unknown extensions.
acceptance_criteria: JSON string array [{"content":"a"},{"content":"b"}] adds exactly 2 rows
JSON array of plain strings ["a","b"] adds exactly 2 rows
JSON array with objects lacking 'content' key exits 1 with descriptive error
CSV with --column text adds one row per data row; other columns appear in metadata JSON
CSV without --column flag exits 1 with a clear message
memory.py ingest file.xyz exits 1 with 'unsupported format' message

handoff_summary.completed: Added _ingest_json(), _ingest_csv(), and refactored _ingest_text_chunks() helpers. cmd_ingest now dispatches on .txt/.md/.json/.csv and falls through to an explicit unsupported-format sys.exit(1). Added --column argument to the ingest subparser.
handoff_summary.risks: csv.DictReader reads the entire file into memory before inserting — fine for typical memory files but could be slow for very large CSVs. Not a concern for current use case.
handoff_summary.next_action: Hand off to tester agent to validate all six acceptance criteria.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — changes are confined to cmd_ingest and three new private helpers in memory.py. No shared state or schema changes.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Extracted _ingest_text_chunks() to avoid duplicating the chunk/filter/insert loop. CSV uses stdlib csv.DictReader — no new dependency. JSON validation is eager (all rows checked before any DB write) so the DB is never partially populated on bad input.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: All six acceptance criteria map to distinct code paths: JSON string branch, JSON object branch, JSON missing-content branch, CSV happy path, CSV no-column branch, unknown-extension branch.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: CSV column-not-found error is detected only after the file header is read; empty CSV (no header row) yields a generic "appears to be empty" message rather than column-specific feedback.

conflict_risks: None — changes are confined to cmd_ingest and three new private helpers in memory.py. No shared state or schema changes.

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Python` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: `python -m py_compile`.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `pytest` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
